title: Preterite and imperfect: telling the war

sections.content: You know the *preterite* and the *imperfect* from A2 Unit 22. The preterite tells what happened, step by step (*llamó*, *capturaron*); the imperfect gives the background that was true at the time (*era cura*, *eran pobres*). A war story needs both.

items.spanish: Hidalgo era cura de Dolores cuando llamó a la población a levantarse.
items.english: Hidalgo was the priest of Dolores when he called the people to rise.

items.spanish: Muchos campesinos eran pobres, y por eso siguieron a Hidalgo.
items.english: Many peasants were poor, and so they followed Hidalgo.

items.spanish: Los realistas tenían un ejército mejor, y en 1811 capturaron a Hidalgo.
items.english: The royalists had a better army, and in 1811 they captured Hidalgo.

items.spanish: La guerra continuaba cuando Iturbide y Guerrero firmaron el Plan de Iguala.
items.english: The war was still going on when Iturbide and Guerrero signed the Plan of Iguala.

sections.content: Ask: is it a step in the story (preterite) or the scene around it (imperfect)? *Cuando llamó* is the event; *era cura* is the situation.
